what: Two questions asked twice by Luai's orchestrator and never answered. Answered here from the repository alone, no compute.

q1_did_arm_CR_ever_finish_or_score_and_w.answer: No. It launched, trained, and was killed by my own cap guard at 14M of 349,999,104 steps. It never produced a checkpoint, a rollout or a score, and it was never relaunched.
q1_did_arm_CR_ever_finish_or_score_and_w.launched: three boxes, six clips (e04 e05 e07 e09 e19 e25), two per box, under the $20 cap Luai set
q1_did_arm_CR_ever_finish_or_score_and_w.the_term_itself_worked: contact_role_palm was confirmed non-zero and finite 13 minutes into the first cells by reading the live offline .wandb stream (brev/read_wandb_terms.py), rather than waiting 40 minutes for the first checkpoint. So the arm's own implementation was verified; only its runs were lost.
q1_did_arm_CR_ever_finish_or_score_and_w.how_it_died: The inline cap guard armed over the launch had the box start time hardcoded as an epoch that was a year out -- 1761612220 is 2025-10-28, not 2026. It computed 26,280 box-hours and $17,871 against the $20 cap and deleted all three boxes, which were at 100% GPU, 14M steps in, and passing every check (commit dd27017).
q1_did_arm_CR_ever_finish_or_score_and_w.spend: about $0.95, plus an hour of wall clock
q1_did_arm_CR_ever_finish_or_score_and_w.why_it_was_never_relaunched: The remaining credit went to Tier 3 reconstruction, the donor transfer and the ORI-W arm, each of which had a cheaper per-clip price. CR appears in no row of results/second_wave_results.md because it has no row to appear in.
q1_did_arm_CR_ever_finish_or_score_and_w.status_now: Fully implemented, staged and gated: brev/patch_contact_role.py, brev/stage_cr.sh, brev/verify_cr_box.sh, the registered bar in docs/ARM_CR.md, and the fixed guard (brev/cr_cap_guard.sh, which now refuses to delete when its own arithmetic is implausible). One command from running: brev/second_wave.sh --groups CR --go --cap 20
q1_did_arm_CR_ever_finish_or_score_and_w.what_it_would_cost_to_answer: $20 for the six clips at 2 per box over 3 boxes, or $7 for two clips on one box as a read on the mechanism

q2_what_was_the_t1_eval_driver_bug.answer: The driver ran one clip of thirty and reported success. Commit 800e36c: 'The eval ran 1 clip of 30 and called it finished: docker exec ate the plan' -- the per-clip plan was passed into docker exec in a way that consumed it, so the loop saw a single clip and exited 0.
three_other_bugs_on_the_same_box: dd427ee -- the eval image did not carry the patches the checkpoints were trained with, so it could not load them
2126c20 -- the eval did not survive that box type, and was deleting boxes that had been marked keep
a65487e -- the upload step was the one step without an SSH retry, and losing it cost a whole box
q2_what_was_the_t1_eval_driver_bug.did_the_bugs_invalidate_the_result: No, and that was checked rather than assumed: the final run covered all 30 clips, every clip's rigid-frame check came out at or below 1.7e-05 cm and 5e-06 deg, and only the reference parquet differed between arms (results/t1_clean_input_eval.json).
q2_what_was_the_t1_eval_driver_bug.the_result: Driving the 30 shipped actors with the clean Tier 1 reference made them worse, not better: mean kit AUC 0.46523 -> 0.28937, SP-SR 0.667 -> 0.133, 2 of 30 clips improved. Each actor learned one specific reference, so a cleaner but different one is a distribution shift. That is the argument for fine-tuning onto it (brev/patch_warm_start.py), not for swapping it cold.
q2_what_was_the_t1_eval_driver_bug.the_one_control_still_owed_and_why_it_ma: A 2-clip Tier 2-input control (e00, e03) through the same patched eval image, expecting the shipped 0.5178 and 0.7806. It costs about $0.70 and it is the only thing that would rule out the eval image itself as the cause. If the image were at fault the clean-input conclusion is wrong and there is a free Tier 1 gain sitting in rollouts we already own, so this is cheap insurance on a conclusion the roadmap leans on. It belongs at the front of the funded queue, before the $7 donor test.
